title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 201
paragraphs: King Xerxes, then, was encamped within the region of Trachis in the Malian land, and the Greeks within the pass. This place is called by the Greeks in general Thermopylae, but by the local inhabitants and those who dwell around it, Pylai. Both sides were encamped in this vicinity; the one held all the country beyond Trachis toward the north, and the others the country stretching toward the south and midday on this side of the continent.
